newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finance minister urges calm after tax vote.
newsitem.headline: Polish finance minister urges calm after tax vote.

text.p: Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said the government would resolve the disarray into which Poland's finances plunged on Thursday when parliament decided to cut income tax for those on low incomes.

"I suggest we all stay calm...the situation is complex but with deliberation we have overcame difficult situations in the past," he said after the lower house voted to cut the lowest tax level to 17 percent next year from the current 21 percent.

He had earlier said such a reduction would cost next year's budget about 4.5 billion zlotys in lost revenues, which would entail a steep cut in spending or increasing the budget gap. ent's sudden decision undermined the government's nearly ready budget draft, due to go to parliament next week, which envisaged keeping the deficit at 2.8 percent of gross domestic prodcut and a cut in the 1997 inflation to 13 percent from 17 percent planned for this year.
But Kolodko said he would cope with the situation.
"With Prime Minister (Wlodzimierz) Cimoszewicz we will certainly propose solutions," he told reporters without elaborating.
The 17-percent tax for the numerous low-paid was unexpectedly approved by the joint forces of the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller group in the government coalition, and opposition parties.
They passed a bill cutting the 1997 tax levels to 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent from the current 21, 33 and 45 percent.
Cimoszewicz's ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), to which Kolodko is linked, wanted the levels to be reduced to 20, 31 and 43 percent.
A senior SLD leader, Leszek Miller, suggested that his party might try to block the tax bill when it is debated in the Senate, Poland's upper house.
"The bill that leaves the lower house today does not end the legislative process," he told PAP news agency.
As a last resort, the SLD could ask President Aleksander Kwasniewski, the SLD's former leader, to veto the tax bill.
Miller denied rumours in Poland's parliament that Kolodko's dismissal was under consideration. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
